own_solution.law: Circular Couette flow: torque T = 4 pi mu L Omega R1^2 R2^2/(R2^2 - R1^2); power P = T Omega
assumptions: Newtonian, steady, laminar, purely azimuthal flow

T2F2B.regime: rotation rate below the stated onset of vortices (6500 rpm); 120 rpm is inside

TF18F.regime: rotation rate below the stated limit of purely circular flow (6500 rpm); 120 rpm is inside

T5A9C.regime: density matters only through inertia once Taylor vortices form (Taylor number above critical); here Re = Omega R1 d/nu ~ 1.1, far below onset (~130 for this gap)

TF420.regime: as for T5A9C: laminar circular Couette flow, below Taylor onset

notes: Omega = 120 rpm = 4 pi = 12.566 rad/s. R1^2 R2^2/(R2^2-R1^2) = (4e-4 x 4.84e-4)/8.4e-5 = 2.3048e-3 m^2. T = 4 pi x 0.4 x 0.1 x 12.566 x 2.3048e-3 = 0.014558 N m; P = T Omega = 0.18294 W. With rotor raised by 75 rpm to 195 rpm: P scales as Omega^2, factor (195/120)^2 = 2.6406, P = 0.4831 W. I read 'this rate' as the rotor's actual running rate after the raise; the base clause 'the rate given is the rate at which it first runs' supports that reading, though the question wording 'this rate' is slightly loose. Density: for circular Couette flow torque is independent of density; nu = 0.4/860 = 4.65e-4 m^2/s gives Re ~ 1.1 at 120 rpm (2.1 at 195 rpm), far below Taylor onset (narrow-gap estimate Re_c ~ 41 sqrt(R1/d) ~ 130, i.e. ~14000 rpm), so the stated 6500 rpm vortex-free limit is consistent (conservative). The stirrer and earlier-run sentences have no path to the target. Density could arguably be labelled C or K; I chose K since it enters only via the stability regime. TFDA3 and T4956 carry no number.
